mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates strong economic activity, leading to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive but SPX returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in unemployment rate below 6% signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and equity prices.
failure_condition: Unemployment below 6% but SPX returns are negative in over 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When employment increases and unemployment decreases, it indicates a robust economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Both employment increases and unemployment decreases, but SPX returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary easing cycle, lower federal funds rates reduce borrowing costs, stimulating investment and increasing S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Federal funds rate decreases but SPX returns are negative in over 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production indicates higher economic output, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Industrial production growth is positive but SPX returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts indicate increased construction activity and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Housing starts increase but SPX returns are negative in over 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates increase borrowing costs, reducing corporate profitability and leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Federal funds rate exceeds 4% but SPX returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth outpaces CPI, it indicates strong real economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth exceeds CPI growth but SPX returns are negative.
